- **the away side moneyline (+114, LowVig.ag)** -- [6093c1cf8a6d6c08] event=85b75fcab1b69e0a4e414382b9f1cc7e selection_id=b5670c82188aefcf edge_bps=None p_model_provenance=none grade=A
  - because: Backing the away side of the moneyline because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) the share of pitches the opposing starter throws with his single most-used offering (primary_pitch_share; each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 45.2%, home 29.1% (this game's own values rest on: away over 1,672 pitches; home over 8,620 pitches); a gap of 16.1 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 9.7 percentage points (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,061 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the away side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: concentration in one pitch is predictability: the more of a starter's arsenal is a single offering, the more of the lineup's preparation transfers, and pitch-level lean is not a term in any club-level price. This is a signal count, not a forecast: it publishes no probability of its own, says nothing about whether the market's price is mistaken, and attaches no claim of value -- none has been earned. (Strategy: evolab genome 6093c1cf8a6d6c08.)
